address: Haarlemmerweg 778-938, Amsterdam (Westerpark corner of the Haarlemmerweg corridor): a 2023 dark-brick high-rise, 12 storeys, tall narrow windows and recessed loggias with pale soffits, a glazed ground floor on a paved square

walls.street: north front on the paved square off the Haarlemmerweg, with the glazed entrance bay

notes: Haarlemmerweg 778-938 (BAG pand 0363100012250971, built 2023, 749 m2, eaves 36.5 m, 12 storeys at 3.0 m). Photographed only after completion, on one day: the north wall at 9.4 m (recording_2025-07-01_09-03-48_00779, 3.6 deg obliquity, 46% foliage from the trees on the square) and the west/east walls from 56-57 m (recording_2025-07-01_09-03-48_00768 at 38 deg and ...00792 at 22.6 deg, 37% and 53% foliage). The 2019 and 2022 crops of the north wall show the low 1980s office block this tower replaced, so they are not evidence.

walls[0] = panel 7 (north, surface 10, 21.4 m): dark charcoal brick, a grid of tall narrow windows with near-black frames, deep recessed loggias (dark, with pale slab soffits) on the upper floors, and a glazed ground floor with the entrance on the paved square. walls[1] = panel 0 (west, surfaces 1 and 5, 29.8 m) and walls[2] = panels 2 and 4 (east, surfaces 3 and 4 plus the 9.8 m return 7) carry the same dark brick grid; the east face is the one with the stacked projecting balcony boxes seen in the 2025 panorama. walls[3] = panel 1 (south, surface 2, 21.8 m, party wall for 9 m): same treatment, no panorama of its own.

Simplified: the recessed loggias are drawn as glass-railed balcony slabs on the south group only (the kit projects balconies, it cannot recess one); the east face's projecting balcony boxes are punched windows and piers, which loses their depth. Not drawn: the step in the north facade where the tower meets its lower base, and the panel joints.
